statement_record.book: The characteristic function of a subset S ⊆ X is ψ_S : X → {0,1}, sending elements of S to the truth value and everything else to the other; each subset S ⊆ X is the pullback of the monomorphism t : {0} → {0,1} along ψ_S, and this square determines S. evidence.intree_statement:
Section SubobjectClassifier.
Context {C : Category}.
Context `{HT : @Terminal C}.
...
Class SubobjectClassifier := {
  Ω : C;                                (* the object of truth values *)
  truth : 1 ~> Ω;                       (* the generic subobject *)

  (* the characteristic morphism of a mono m : u ~> x *)
  char {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω;

  (* the classifying square is a pullback of truth along char m *)
  char_pullback {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) :
    IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one;

  (* and char m is the unique morphism with that property *)
  char_unique {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) (h : x ~> Ω) :
    IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M
}.

Lemma truth_monic : Monic truth.
(* line 72 *) Definition truth_subobject : SubObj Ω :=
  {| sub_dom := 1; sub_mono := truth; sub_is_monic := truth_monic |}.   (* 'the universal monomorphism t may be called truth' *)

Lemma char_respects {u u' x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) ...   (* char depends only on the SUBOBJECT, not on the chosen representing mono; derived from char_pullback + char_unique rather than assumed as a field *)

Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) :
  @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.   (* forward: char; backward: pullback of truth via sub_reindex; both round trips proved (classifier_char_roundtrip, classifier_pullback_roundtrip) *)

statement_record.book: In a category C with a terminal object 1, a subobject classifier is a monomorphism t : 1 → Ω such that every monomorphism m : S ↣ X is a pullback of t in a unique way: for each m there is a unique arrow ψ : X → Ω (the characteristic function of m) making the square on m, the unique S → 1, t and ψ a pullback. The universal monomorphism t may be called 'truth'.
statement_record.intree: `Class SubobjectClassifier`, in a section with `Context {C : Category}` and `Context \`{HT : @Terminal C}`, with fields `Ω : C`, `truth : 1 ~> Ω`, `char {u x} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω`, `char_pullback : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one`, and `char_unique : IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M`. Monicity of `truth` is DERIVED (`truth_monic`), the generic subobject is packaged as `truth_subobject`, and the classification bijection is `classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω)` in Sets.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The in-tree form Skolemizes the book's 'there is a unique ψ' into the operation `char` plus the uniqueness field `char_unique`; because the library's `∃!` is Type-valued (`unique_obj` carries the witness) the two presentations are interderivable. `IsPullback` is the full record (commuting square + universal property with uniqueness), not an apex-only or cone-free weakening -- the trap this library documents elsewhere (apex-only `PreservesLimit`) is absent here. The book's requirement that t be monic is derived, not assumed, which is no weaker. The class is if anything slightly richer than the book's definition: `char_respects` (char is well defined on subobject classes) and `classifier_classifies` (the SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) bijection the book's 'this square determines S' gestures at) are proved consequences. Hypothesis parity: the class needs only `Terminal C`; `HasPullbacks C` is a section hypothesis used solely by `classifier_classifies`, matching the book, which does not require C to have all pullbacks.

Definition Pow {C : Category} {H : ElementaryTopos C} (a : C) : C := Ω ^ a.
(* line 146 *) Definition relations_iso {C : Category} {H : ElementaryTopos C} (a b : C) :
  @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj (a × b) |} {| carrier := a ~> Pow b |} :=
  iso_compose exp_iso (classifier_classifies (a × b)).

statement_record.book: An (elementary) topos is a category E such that (i) E has all finite limits, (ii) E has a subobject classifier, and (iii) E is cartesian closed -- each functor - × b has a right adjoint c ↦ c^b, so hom(a × b, c) ≅ hom(a, c^b) and E has exponentials.
statement_record.intree: `Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category)` with the five fields `topos_terminal : @Terminal C`, `topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C`, `topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C`, `topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian`, `topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal`, where `Closed` IS the exponential adjunction `exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y` plus the beta law. Derived in-file: `Pow a := Ω ^ a` and `relations_iso : SubObj (a × b) ≅ (a ~> Pow b)`. Witness: `FinSet_Topos : ElementaryTopos FinSet`, with `Pow 2 = 4` by `eq_refl`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same (equivalent axiomatization). Clause (iii) is matched literally by `Closed`'s `exp_iso`; clause (ii) by `SubobjectClassifier`. Clause (i) is spelled as terminal object + binary products + pullbacks rather than 'all finite limits'; these cut out the same class of categories (terminal + pullbacks already suffice), so the predicate is neither weaker nor stronger. DISCLOSED API nuance, stated by the file itself (Structure/Topos.v:20-27): 'the reduction of pullbacks to products and equalizers (and conversely) is not formalized in this library, so we do not pretend one component subsumes another, and we deliberately do not add equalizers to the class.' Hence no in-tree lemma derives equalizers or a general finite limit FROM `ElementaryTopos`; a consumer needing 'E has all finite limits' as a usable fact must still build it.

statement_record.book: The category Sets of all small sets is a topos, and so is the category Sets^(C^op) of all set-valued contravariant functors (presheaves) on any small category C.
statement_record.intree: Neither half is proved. What exists: (a) `FinSet_Topos : ElementaryTopos FinSet` -- a genuine, fully computable elementary topos, but of SKELETAL FINITE sets, not of all sets; (b) for `Sets` (setoids): `Sets_Terminal`, `Sets_Cartesian`, `Sets_Closed` as instances, plus the classifier content as the cross-universe theorems `sets_char_pullback` / `sets_char_unique` / `sets_char_subobject` -- but no `HasPullbacks Sets`, no `SubobjectClassifier Sets`, hence no `ElementaryTopos Sets`; (c) for presheaves: `Presheaves := [U^op, C]` exists as a category and `Functor_Category_Cartesian` supplies pointwise products, and nothing more.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the book's assertion is in force for neither half. 'Sets is a topos' is blocked by a DOCUMENTED and deliberate universe obstruction (Instance/Sets/Classifier.v:29-45: morphism `≈` is Type-valued, so the truth-value setoid must be `Type@{o}` under iffT, one universe up, and the one-level `IsPullback` form is not statable). 'Presheaf categories are toposes' has no in-tree content beyond pointwise products; the assertion appears only as background prose (Theory/Sheaf.v:84).

statement_record.book: A functor F : C^op → Sets is called a presheaf on C. Motivating topological case: C the poset of open sets of a space X, so F assigns to each open U a set F(U) functorially in inclusions (e.g. the continuous real-valued functions on U); the sheaves among these are central in algebraic geometry and topology (the sheaf condition itself is not stated at this point in the book).
statement_record.intree: `Definition Presheaf (U C : Category) := U^op ⟶ C.` together with `Definition Presheaves {U C : Category} := [U^op, C].` The book's Sets-valued case is `Presheaf C Sets`, which is exactly the type the in-tree `Class Sheaf` quantifies over.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger (strictly more general): the in-tree definition is parametric in the value category C, of which the book's Sets-valued notion is the instance `Presheaf C Sets`; the dual `Copresheaf`/`Copresheaves` is defined as well, and the associated category `[U^op, C]` is exactly the book's presheaf category. Regarding the surrounding motivation (not itself a mathematical claim): the library goes FURTHER than the book's paragraph in one direction -- the sheaf condition IS formalized, via `Class Site` and `Class Sheaf`, with `Sheaves` the full subcategory of presheaves and `sheaf_iso_closed` its repleteness -- and stops short in another: the specific site of open sets of a topological space, and the sheaf of continuous real-valued functions, are not instantiated (Instance/Poset.v gives posets as categories generically but no lattice of opens). Note also the disclosed donor erratum on the `Sheaf` predicate recorded in Theory/Sheaf/Category.v's header; it does not touch the presheaf definition itself.
